from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: The Transformation Perspective", 
                          ["Matrices act as functions moving the entire coordinate plane.", 
                           "A matrix A transforms a vector v into w.", 
                           "Think of this as a transformation of the grid."])
        
        # Load asset
        grid_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        
        # Define objects
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], x_length=4, y_length=4)
        v_vec = Vector([1, 1], color=YELLOW)
        
        # Matrix to transform
        matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]] # Shear matrix
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'B2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.75)
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_asset.move_to(grid.get_center())), Create(grid), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(v_vec, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7)
        v_label = self.add_labeled_vector(v_vec, "v", position='top_right', offset=0.2)
        self.play(Create(v_vec), Write(v_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Animate the grid transformation
        target_grid = grid.copy().apply_matrix(matrix)
        target_v = v_vec.copy().apply_matrix(matrix)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(grid, target_grid),
            Transform(v_vec, target_v),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Composition means applying one transformation after another.",
            "We apply B first, then A to result C.",
            "We want a single matrix C for AB.",
            "Robotic arm rotates then extends its reach.",
            "This sequence equals a combined transformation matrix."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Function Composition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load asset
        robot_arm = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(robot_arm, 'B5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(robot_arm))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Rotate arm (B)
        self.play(Rotate(robot_arm, angle=PI/4, about_point=robot_arm.get_center()), run_time=1)
        # Extend arm (A) - simple scale or move
        self.play(robot_arm.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        matrix_c = MathTex("C = AB", color="#FF00FF")
        formula_label = Text("Resulting Matrix", font_size=20)
        
        self.place_in_area(matrix_c, 'B3', 'C4', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_in_area(formula_label, 'D3', 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(matrix_c), Write(formula_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(robot_arm, 'B5', scale_factor=0.9)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Chain Reaction", [
            "Track the basis vectors i and j.",

            "A then moves those results again.",
            "Final positions define the columns of matrix C.",
            "This chain is the matrix product AB."
        ])

        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], x_length=4, y_length=4, axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], x_length=4, y_length=4)
        
        # Assets
        vector_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vectors.svg")
        
        i_hat = Vector(RIGHT, color="#FF0000") # Asset color requirements
        j_hat = Vector(UP, color="#00FF00")
        
        grid_group = VGroup(grid, axes, i_hat, j_hat)
        self.place_in_area(grid_group, 'C2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(grid), Create(axes), GrowArrow(i_hat), GrowArrow(j_hat))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        b_matrix = [[1.5, 0], [0, 0.7]]
        self.play(
            grid.animate.apply_matrix(b_matrix),
            i_hat.animate.apply_matrix(b_matrix),
            j_hat.animate.apply_matrix(b_matrix)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        a_matrix = [[0, -1], [1, 0]]
        self.play(
            grid.animate.apply_matrix(a_matrix),
            i_hat.animate.apply_matrix(a_matrix),
            j_hat.animate.apply_matrix(a_matrix)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        dot_i = Dot(i_hat.get_end(), color="#FFFF00")
        dot_j = Dot(j_hat.get_end(), color="#FFFF00")

outline.topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Transformation Perspective
sections.content: Recall that a matrix represents a function: it takes a vector 'v' as input and outputs a transformed vector 'w' (w = Av). Visualize this as a grid shift: a matrix A stretches or rotates the entire coordinate plane.
sections.example: Visualizing a 2x2 matrix as a transformation grid that tilts a unit square.

sections.title: The Concept of Function Composition
sections.content: Define composition: If we apply transformation B first, then transformation A, the result is a new 'combined' transformation. We denote this as A(B(v)). The goal is to find a single matrix C such that C = AB.
sections.example: A robotic arm: Matrix B rotates the arm base, and Matrix A extends the reach. Applying them sequentially is equivalent to a single 'combined' reach-and-rotate matrix C.

sections.title: Visualizing the Chain Reaction
sections.content: Focus on the basis vectors (i = [1, 0] and j = [0, 1]). First, B moves i and j to new positions B(i) and B(j). Then, A moves those new vectors again. The final positions of i and j determine the columns of the new matrix C.
sections.example: Animation: Use a 'Grid Monster'. It first stretches the grid (B), then the result is rotated by the next transformation (A). The combined grid movement is the matrix product AB.

sections.title: Deriving the Rule: Why 'Row by Column'?
sections.content: Explain that matrix multiplication is not commutative (AB ≠ BA). It is simply the bookkeeping method to track where the basis vectors end up after two successive mappings.
sections.example: A 2D character (e.g., a cat icon) on a screen: Matrix B scales it, Matrix A reflects it. Demonstrating that flipping then scaling (AB) results in a different final pose than scaling then flipping (BA).

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Reiterate that matrix multiplication is a geometric 'shortcut'. Instead of applying two functions, we multiply the matrices once to capture the entire composite movement of the space.
sections.example: A shortcut for computer graphics engines: Pre-calculating a single 'Combined Matrix' for character movement instead of calculating every frame step-by-step.
